title: Ops Concordat: SLO Activation Microplan
content:
Purpose:
This microplan captures a low-friction, cross-functional approach to activate a set of model-serving SLOs for a first-wave pilot (hosted-api + dedicated). The focus is coordination (the ‘concordat’) between product owners, platform, SRE, and oncall so that SLOs are actionable, observable, and have clear handoff/runbook artifacts.

Context and rationale:
- Problem: engineering teams have defined target availability/latency SLOs but operational readiness (dashboards, runbooks, incident triggers) is inconsistent across services.
- Hypothesis: a lightweight, repeatable activation pattern reduces deployment friction and reduces false alarms by 30% within the pilot cohort.
- Scope for this microplan: 6 pilot services (mix of hosted-api routes and dedicated model pools); target duration: 8 weeks.

Objectives (SMART):
1) For pilot services, publish an SLO dashboard and a one-page runbook template within 3 weeks of kickoff.
2) Reduce paging noise by 25% through improved alert thresholds and multi-signal checks by end of pilot (week 8).
3) Validate auto-fallback routing policy for two high-traffic routes during a controlled failover test (week 6).
4) Document lessons and a handoff checklist so two additional teams can onboard in <2 weeks post-pilot.

Stakeholders and roles (concordat):
- SRE lead (owner): Aisha Patel — program owner, weekly sync facilitator, decision arbiter for incident/alert thresholds.
- Platform eng: Marco Ruiz — telemetry instrumentation, Grafana templates, data retention knobs.
- Product / Hosted API PM: Lena Thompson — defines customer-impact mapping and SLA translation to SLOs.
- Serving runtime / Model ops: Priya Nair — validates fallback paths and model-variant compatibility.
- Oncall champions (per service): names TBD — responsible for runbook smoke tests.

Success signals (how we’ll know it worked):
- Dashboards show correct SLI ingestion for 95% of sampled requests (no missing metrics).
- Oncall runbook template used for at least 5 real incidents during pilot with accurate postmortems.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) improves by 15% for SLO-related pages.
- Stakeholder survey (NPS-style) shows >= +20 net promoter change on operational confidence post-pilot.

High-level timeline and milestones (week numbers from kickoff 2026-01-19):
- Week 0 (2026-01-19): Kickoff + sync with service owners. Confirm pilot cohort.
- Week 1 (2026-01-26): Telemetry audit complete (instrumentation gaps identified).
- Week 2 (2026-02-02): Dashboard and alert template v0 deployed to dev.
- Week 3 (2026-02-09): Runbook one-pager drafted and approved for first two services.
- Week 4 (2026-02-16): Alert tuning workshop; reduce noisy alerts.
- Week 6 (2026-03-02): Controlled failover and fallback routing test; collect metrics.
- Week 8 (2026-03-16): Pilot retro, playbook finalized, onboarding checklist published.

Deliverables (minimum viable set):
- SLO spec per service (customer-impact mapping, SLI definitions, objective levels).
- Grafana dashboard + Loki/Prometheus query snippets stored in the shared dashboard folder.
- Runbook one-pager template with triage flow, mitigation steps, and escalation contact matrix.
- Alert tuning guide with example thresholds and multi-signal logic.
- Test plan for fallback routing (step-by-step, validation criteria).

Operational details / instrumentation checklist (quick checklist to run for each service):
- Verify: request + response latency histograms, error rate (5xx and model-specific errors), queue/backpressure metrics present.
- Validate: normalized token counting (hosted-api) for cost-aware SLI.
- Confirm: KV cache hit ratio metrics capture (for caching SLOs).
- Set: sampling rules for traces to keep storage reasonable but preserve tail latency signals.
- Deploy: feature flags for turning on/off fallback routing per-route.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly 30-minute sync (Tuesday 10am PT) — updates from SRE, platform, and product.
- Daily 15-minute standups during failover test week.
- Slack playbook channel: #ops-concordat-slo (use for rollout decisions and triage shortcuts).
- Confluence page (linked_artifact above) holds canonical spec and templates.

Runbook template (one-pager outline):
- Title + owner + oncall rotation links
- Quick indicators (what to look for in dashboard)
- Immediate mitigation steps (run commands, common restart sequences, known safe fallbacks)
- Fallback routing execution (how to flip to variant, validation checks)
- Escalation contacts + Postmortem owner

Failover/fallback test plan (summary):
- Goal: exercise automatic and manual fallback for two model routes, measure impact on latency/quality and system stability.
- Preconditions: canary traffic route active; fallback variant is compatible and pinned.
- Steps:
  1) Inject synthetic latency to primary model pool for 10 minutes (rate-limited).
  2) Observe SLI degradation and automatic policy decision (if implemented).
  3) Execute manual fallback (if auto not triggered); measure time-to-stable and error rate.
  4) Rollback to primary; measure recovery.
- Validation: no customer-facing errors >1% sustained; tail latency within target after fallback.

Risk register (short-form):
- Risk: telemetry gaps lead to blind spots. Mitigation: telemetry audit and preflight checklist.
- Risk: fallback introduces semantic regressions for responses. Mitigation: small-scale A/B quality checks and manual review by model owners.
- Risk: paging storm during testing. Mitigation: temporary suppression windows with clear owners and escalation path.

Open questions / decisions to resolve (notes to self):
- Which exact SLI percentile(s) do we standardize on for tokenized latency? p50/p95/p99 — propose p95 & p99 for alerts, p50 for capacity context.
- Retention policy for SLO signal data in observability: default 30 days for pilot, confirm costs.
- Define acceptable customer-impact threshold for automatic fallback (absolute vs relative).

Action items (owners + next steps):
- Aisha: schedule kickoff, invite service owners, confirm cohort by 2026-01-16 (DONE).
- Marco: run telemetry audit and post findings to confluence by 2026-01-23.
- Lena: draft customer-impact mapping templates and review with feature PMs by 2026-01-28.
- Priya: stage fallback variants in dedicated pool and validate compatibility by 2026-02-06.
- Oncall champions: run the runbook smoke test on staging after dashboards are live and report pass/fail.

Retrospective checklist (for end of pilot):
- Collect metrics: paging volume, MTTA, SLO burn rates (before/after).
- Collect anecdotes: 3-4 curated incidents where runbook was followed.
- Decide: which elements are core to the long-form playbook vs optional.

Notes & informal context (scratchpad):
- Keep the process light: aim for artifacts that teams will actually use (one-page runbooks beat multi-page docs).
- Emphasize cross-team rehearsals rather than documentation-only onboarding.
- Expect to iterate on thresholds — treat week 4 tuning as normal.

Draft of email to stakeholders (template):
Subject: Pilot kickoff: Ops Concordat SLO activation (Jan 19)
Body: Hi all — quick note that we’re kicking off a short pilot to standardize SLO activation across a small set of model-serving routes. Goal is to ship dashboards, runbooks, and a controlled fallback test in ~8 weeks. Please see the attached confluence spec and add your service to the cohort by EOD Friday. We’ll meet weekly Tuesday 10am PT.

Appendix: useful links and quick commands
- Dashboard folder: /dashboards/reliability/pilot-ops-concordat
- FAQ: link to common SLO questions on Confluence (linked above)
- Common queries: (examples included in dashboard templates)

-- end of microplan (working draft).
